extracted.intended_audience: executive branch agency acquisition/procurement officials, program managers, agency heads, GSA/OFPP staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for federal agencies on applying OMB Circular A-109 to the planning, solicitation, evaluation, development, demonstration, production, testing, and budgeting of major system acquisitions (ADP, construction, demonstration projects, weapon systems, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Top level management attention to determination of agency mission needs and goals
rubrics_metrics.description: "Top level management attention to the determination of agency mission needs and goals."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directive from the Circular: agency heads must give priority involvement in identifying mission needs and goals; this is a required principle underlying the major system acquisition process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrated systematic approach for establishing mission needs, budgeting, contracting, and managing programs
rubrics_metrics.description: "An integrated systematic approach for establishing mission needs, budgeting, contracting, and managing programs."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should coordinate mission analysis, budget planning, contracting strategy, and program management so decisions occur in a total-system context rather than in isolated silos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early direction of research and development efforts to satisfy mission needs and goals
rubrics_metrics.description: "Early direction of research and development efforts to satisfy mission needs and goals."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R&D should be guided early by mission needs so technology development is aligned with program objectives and avoids later misalignment or wasted effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improved opportunities for innovative private sector contributions to national needs
rubrics_metrics.description: "Improved opportunities for innovative private sector contributions to national needs."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solicitations and acquisition strategies should encourage industry innovation and competition (e.g., solicit in mission terms, avoid unnecessary spec constraints).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of premature commitments to full-scale development and production
rubrics_metrics.description: "Avoidance of premature commitments to full-scale development and production."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use phased approach (exploration, demonstrations, then full-scale development) and require key agency head decisions before committing major resources to production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early communication with Congress in the acquisition process
rubrics_metrics.description: "Early communication with Congress in the acquisition process by relating major system acquisitions to agency mission needs and goals."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicate approved mission needs during the budget process (A-10/A-11) so Congress can consider major needs and initiation decisions early, prior to large commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency discretion to prescribe additional criteria/relative dollar thresholds for major system classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies "may... prescribe additional criteria and/or relative dollar thresholds for determining which agency programs are to be classified [as] major systems" and may set different thresholds for different types (e.g., ADP, construction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency-specific thresholds and criteria are allowed to reflect management attention and program categories; agencies should document and apply them consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing analysis of mission capabilities, technological opportunities, priorities, and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB A-109 "requires a continuing analysis of current and forecasted mission capabilities, technological opportunities, overall priorities, and resources that are involved."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must periodically reassess capabilities and opportunities; identification of deficiencies or opportunities leads to a formal mission need statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission need statement content and form
rubrics_metrics.description: The mission need statement "includes the mission purpose, capability, agency components involved, time constraints, value or worth of meeting the need, relative priority, and operating constraints, and is not to be expressed in terms of equipment or other means which might satisfy the need."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft mission need statements in capability/mission terms (not equipment). It should document purpose, stakeholders, timeframe, priority and constraints; it is submitted to the agency head for approval (first key decision).

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of a Program Manager early
rubrics_metrics.description: A "program manager should be designated for each major system acquisition program as soon as possible after the mission need decision to explore alternative system design concepts."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign a program manager early to lead exploration; the manager should recruit a skilled team and have continuity/tenure to accrue accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program manager qualifications and charter
rubrics_metrics.description: The program manager "ideally should be a multidiscipline, experienced manager with sufficient tenure and interest..."; program objectives "are required to be incorporated in a written charter, which defines the authority, responsibility, and accountability of the program manager."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a written charter specifying authority, responsibility, accountability, program objectives (capability, cost, schedule) and ensure organization/management level matches program importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop an acquisition strategy that forms the basis for a system acquisition plan
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the program manager's first tasks is to "develop an acquisition strategy... The strategy should form the basis for the program manager's system acquisition plan."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategy should not be a cookbook—tailor it to program goals, schedule decision points, contingencies, measurement of accomplishments, and time-phased near-term actions; refine as knowledge accrues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of private sector and contracting as tools (A-76)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategy considerations include "the general policy to rely on the private sector in accordance with OMB Circular No. A-76; the use of contracting as a tool in the acquisition process and not as a substitute for management."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on private sector solutions when appropriate, but retain government management responsibility; avoid outsourcing oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of competitive parallel short-term planned dollar value contracts during exploration
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy to use "competitive parallel short-term planned dollar value contracts for well-defined work activities during exploration of system design concept alternatives."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award multiple short-term contracts to broaden alternatives, reduce technical uncertainties, encourage competition and innovation during exploration phases; avoid nonessential contractor paperwork requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: System/product development considerations (risk sharing, tailoring specs, use of labs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples include recognition of risks/uncertainties to assure proper risk sharing; Government tailoring of specifications and standards; time-phased introduction of results; government guidelines for contractor development of performance specs; optimal use of government laboratories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance risk sharing between government and contractors; avoid constraining contractors with onerous specs; use labs for technical direction and to support contractor performance where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business management considerations (competition, lead times, avoid 'auctions')
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples include obtaining and sustaining competition (including high-cost subsystems), accommodating procurement lead times, precluding technical transfusions and 'auctions' in proposal evaluation, and providing contracts for proposal submittals for next planned increments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design acquisition processes to sustain competition, account for procurement lead times, avoid practices that unfairly advantage bidders (auctions/transfusions), and plan for follow-on proposals contractually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program management organizational choices and incremental approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples include selection of a project management organizational mode (vertical or matrix), the appropriateness of incremental approvals of contractors' efforts throughout the acquisition process, and applicability of standardization/interoperability policies with friendly countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose an organizational model that fits program needs; use incremental approvals where appropriate; consider standardization/interoperability requirements early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation in terms of mission need (not equipment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicitation "should explain the need in mission or capability terms (not equipment terms)..." and contractors "should be free to propose their own technical approach, main design features, subsystems, and alternatives to schedule, cost, and capability goals."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write solicitations to describe capabilities, schedule objectives, program costs, operating constraints, and background; avoid restricting contractors by referencing Government specs/standards; identify available government information and encourage industry innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry outreach and broad solicitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are "encouraged to conduct orientation briefings for industry, and, where appropriate, allow industry to comment on a draft of the solicitation and the system acquisition strategy." Solicitations "are to be sent to a broad base of qualified firms, and participation of smaller and newer businesses is encouraged."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use briefings and draft comments to remove inhibitors to innovation; actively solicit a broad and diverse set of firms, including small/new businesses, and primarily solicit private industry (while considering other sources).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of government laboratories and not-for-profits in solicitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Government laboratories, FFRDCs, educational institutions and not-for-profits "may also be considered as sources for alternative system design concepts... When [they] submit... care must be taken to exclude such proposers from the evaluation process. If further exploration... that concept should be made available to industry to propose on the continued development stages. Direct competition between industry and government laboratories must be avoided."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid conflicts of interest and direct competition between government research entities and industry; if lab concepts are pursued further, make them available for industry proposals on later stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals should be evaluated considering: capability to meet mission need and program objectives (including resources required); benefits from trade-offs among technical performance, acquisition costs, ownership costs, and time to develop/procure; and relevant accomplishment record and competence of competitors' key personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use expert review teams (internal and external) to evaluate proposals against mission capability, cost/time trade-offs, and proposer past performance and personnel competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallel short-term contracts: objectives and evaluation emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Parallel short-term contracts expand concepts and reduce technical uncertainties; emphasis during contract performance should be on providing contractors relevant operational/support experience, measures to progressively reduce risks, responsiveness to mission need, benefits to the Government, and continuous evaluation to permit elimination of least attractive alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractors should identify risk areas and propose risk reduction activities; agencies should supply demonstration/test criteria and life-cycle cost factors to support contractor planning; avoid constraining innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive demonstrations: purpose and contractor obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Competitive demonstrations "are intended to verify that the chosen concepts are sound, perform in an operational environment, and provide a basis for selection..." Demonstration contracts should provide for contractors to submit proposals for full-scale development and initial production and furnish operational test conditions, mission performance criteria, and life cycle cost factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use prototypes/limited development models to verify concepts; require contractors to prepare end-item performance specs, identify tailoring of specs/standards, recommend tailoring of management systems requirements, and propose contract data lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for full-scale development/initial production
rubrics_metrics.description: System(s) and contractor(s) selection for full-scale development should be made on the basis of: essential system concept performance measured against mission need and program objectives; an evaluation of remaining risks and potential resolutions; an evaluation of estimated acquisition and ownership costs; and factors such as the contractor's demonstrated management, financial, and technical capabilities to meet program objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection decisions (third key decision) must weigh performance, residual risk, life-cycle costs, and contractor capabilities; document rationale and reaffirm mission need and objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program manager monitoring and variance handling
rubrics_metrics.description: The program manager is required to monitor program progress as well as contractor progress in fulfilling contract performance, cost, and schedule commitments. "Significant actual or forecast variances from plan are to be analyzed and alternatives considered with resultant actions or recommendation for actions brought to the attention of the appropriate contractor or government management authority."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish monitoring processes and escalate significant variances with analysis and recommended corrective actions to appropriate authorities promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent testing of initial production units
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial production units are to be tested and evaluated in an environment that assures effective performance in expected operational conditions. "Normally the testing is to be done independent of the agency's development and user organizations." Exceptions require agency head authorization for impracticability or extreme urgency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for independent operational testing separate from development/user organizations unless a justified exception is approved by the agency head.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production authorization (fourth key decision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Following satisfactory test results and reconfirmation of mission need and program objectives, the agency head may authorize full production (the fourth key decision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure reconfirmation of need and objectives and satisfactory independent testing before authorizing full production; document decision basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application to ADP systems (GSA interface, combining decisions for off‑the‑shelf)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application to ADP systems follows established procedures involving coordination/approval by GSA and OMB. If selection involves procurement of off-the-shelf equipment, the second and third key agency head decisions may be combined. The fourth key decision normally does not apply except for multiple-quantity procurements of newly developed ADP systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate responsibilities with GSA early; adapt the general process appropriately for ADP peculiarities and established GSA/OMB procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application to construction projects (analyze alternatives, use short-term A&E contracts)
rubrics_metrics.description: For construction, analysis should consider best economic use of property and alternatives (excess space, joint use, purchase, lease, new construction). Short-term competitive A&E contracts should be awarded to explore alternative design concepts; production decision (fourth key decision) usually not involved for single-quantity construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use competitive A&E exploration, consider scale models or modules for untried techniques, and resolve executive agent responsibilities with GSA at outset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application to demonstration projects (exceptions to competitive demonstration, no production decision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstration projects follow the general process except the fourth key decision (production) — production would be undertaken by private sector. A-109 provides for an exception when competitive demonstration and evaluation is not required; some projects may terminate at completion of the demonstration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor process for demonstration objectives (technology validation rather than production); document exceptions to competition when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain an adequate technology base using government labs and private sector
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency R&D activities should "maintain an adequate base of technology to be responsive to mission needs and available for consideration by private sector suppliers" including research, exploratory design studies, proof of concept, subsystem development, tests/evaluations, and sufficient demonstration to permit application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in technology base activities to field relevant technologies into solicitations; balance government lab and private sector roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government laboratories' supporting roles (solicitation docs, evaluation, risk assessment, independent test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Government laboratories should support program management (when not proposers) by preparing mission-oriented solicitation technical documentation; evaluating alternative design concepts and innovative uses of technology; assessing technical risk; evaluating contractors' technical progress; and conducting independent tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use labs as expert technical support while avoiding conflicts when they propose concepts; labs provide objective evaluation and testing to inform acquisition decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on full-scale subsystem development until system selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsystems that may be candidates for inclusion in a major system acquisition program "are not to be fully developed until the subsystem is identified as a part of a system proposed for full-scale development..." Exceptions permitted for long lead-time generic needs or high potential for common use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid committing to full-scale subsystem development prematurely; permit exceptions for long-lead or broadly applicable subsystems, and allow contractors to propose subsystem incorporation.

rubrics_metrics.name: R&D budget presentation categories for FY 1979 and beyond
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are to identify R&D in three categories: general technology base; specific development efforts in support of alternative system design concepts aggregated by mission; and full-scale development of systems related to mission needs. Circulars A-109 and A-11 require realignment of R&D budgets into these categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare budget displays that separate technology base, exploratory developments aggregated by mission, and full-scale development; agencies may subdivide further if desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of key agency head decisions at defined acquisition milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: The pamphlet describes numbered key decisions (Circle 1: approval of mission need; Circle 2: approval to proceed to competitive demonstrations/reaffirm mission need; Circle 3: authorize full-scale development/initial production; Circle 4: authorize full production) and that these are required agency head approvals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the milestone decision points and obtain agency head approval at each key decision before major commitments; use these decisions to prevent premature commitments and to ensure oversight.
